question: During the turning operation on lathe, if D is the initial diameter and d is the final diameter of the work piece, the depth of cut, t, is calculated by_______.
solution:
The correct answer is __t = (D - d) / 2__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The depth of cut is the amount of material removed from the workpiece during one pass of the cutting tool.
 
• In turning operations on a lathe, the depth of cut is determined by the difference between the initial diameter (D) and the final diameter (d) of the workpiece, divided by 2.
 
• This formula ensures that the depth of cut is measured as the thickness removed from one side of the workpiece.
 
• For example, if the initial diameter is 50 mm and the final diameter is 40 mm, the depth of cut would be (50 - 40) / 2 = 5 mm.
 
• Accurate calculation of the depth of cut is essential for achieving desired dimensions and ensuring efficient material removal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lathe Machine:**

 
 
• A lathe machine is used to perform operations such as turning, facing, threading, and drilling on cylindrical workpieces.
 
• The workpiece is held in a chuck or between centers and rotated while a cutting tool removes material.
 
 
 
• **Turning Operation:**
 
 
• Turning is a machining process in which a cutting tool removes material from the outer diameter of a rotating workpiece.
 
• It is used to produce cylindrical shapes with specific dimensions and surface finishes.
 
 
 
• **Cutting Parameters:**
 
 
• Key cutting parameters in turning operations include spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut.
 
• These parameters must be optimized to achieve desired results and ensure tool life.
